title: Universal scalar comparison identifies the two evaluation-defined finite quotient Hom maps
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, a scheme W and m≤n. Let φ be the actual quotient of finite integral coefficient sheaves O_E/(t^(n+1))→O_E/(t^(m+1)) of [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. For every evaluation-normalized scalar Hom model A furnished by [lem-fix-site-perfect-scalar-hom], let A.scalar.T be its universal derived scalar extension. Let F be the fixed finite quotient derived functor and H_n,H_m its derived internal Homs [def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations, def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. There is a natural isomorphism e:A.scalar.T≅F such that, for every ambient P,Q at level n, the siteScalarHomComparison of A followed by H_m((e_P^-1)^op,e_Q) equals e_(H_n(P,Q)) followed by finiteIntrinsicReductionHom(P,Q). This is an equality of the specified evaluation transposes, not an invertibility assertion; no perfectness is required. All universe choices and components appear verbatim in Lean.

proof.text: The two ordinary scalar operations are the same sheafified balanced tensor functor. Uniqueness of its total left derived functor gives the natural isomorphism e normalized by the universal counits.

The closed tensors have the same specified internal Hom. Their adjunctions give the unique comparison between their left adjoints. Their K-flat model equations identify this comparison and both scalar tensorators on pure tensors; signed total symmetry gives the same conversion from symmetric evaluation to Hom-tensor-P evaluation.

Uncurry the asserted square. Naturality of e and the normalized tensor squares identify both sides with scalar extension of source evaluation. Injectivity of the target adjunction proves the equality. This works for arbitrary ambient P,Q and uses no dualizability or invertibility conclusion.

theorem finiteQuotient_homModel_comparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (W : Scheme.{u}) (m n : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n) :
    letI : EssentiallySmall.{u + 1} W.ProEt := essentiallySmallSelf.{0} _
    letI := integralCoefficientAbSheafify.{u, u} W
    letI := integralCoefficientAbLocallyBijective.{u, u} W
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (RingedTensorModules.{u + 1, u, u}
      (ProEt.topology W) (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E W n))
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (RingedTensorModules.{u + 1, u, u}
      (ProEt.topology W) (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E W m))
    ∀ A : SitePerfectScalarHomData.{u + 1, u, u, u + 2} (ProEt.topology W)
      (coefficientFiniteQuotient l E W h),
    ∃ e : SheafOfModules.DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel.T.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 2, u + 2}
        (SitePerfectScalarHomData.scalar.{u + 1, u, u, u + 2} A) ≅
          coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E W h,
      ∀ P Q : normalizedDVRDerived l E W n,
        siteScalarHomComparison.{u + 1, u, u, u + 2} _ (coefficientFiniteQuotient l E W h) A P Q ≫
            (coefficientFiniteInternalHom l E W m).map
              (Prod.mkHom (e.inv.app P).op (e.hom.app Q)) =
          e.hom.app ((coefficientFiniteInternalHom l E W n).obj (op P, Q)) ≫
            finiteIntrinsicReductionHom l E W h P Q
